subject.title: [Bug]: OpenAI-compatible streaming tool calls are dropped when provider omits finish_reason

question: Should OpenAI-compatible transport treat native `delta.tool_calls` plus a clean SSE `[DONE]` terminal, but no final `finish_reason`, as executable `toolUse` while preserving EOF-without-`[DONE]` fail-closed behavior?
rationale: This changes the condition under which OpenClaw executes provider-supplied tool calls, so automation should not choose the permanent completion contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt clean `[DONE]` contract
options.body: Land or refine the linked PR so native tool calls execute only after an observed clean SSE terminal and remain stripped on truncated EOF or ambiguous visible-text streams.

options.title: Keep explicit finish_reason only
options.body: Reject the no-finish provider compatibility behavior and document that OpenAI-compatible providers must emit a final tool-call finish reason for tool execution.

options.title: Require provider opt-in
options.body: Add an explicit provider/model capability before accepting no-finish clean-stream tool calls, trading compatibility for a narrower execution boundary.

recommendation.title: Adopt clean `[DONE]` contract
recommendation.body: Land or refine the linked PR so native tool calls execute only after an observed clean SSE terminal and remain stripped on truncated EOF or ambiguous visible-text streams.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current guard and tests for this exact stream completion boundary, making them the best history-backed reviewer for the contract choice.
